title: How much of a measured AI preference is the model, and how much is the instrument?
abstract: arXiv:2608.23641v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Model welfare research infers what a model prefers from the answers returned to prompts written to elicit preferences. Keeling et al. (2024), Mazeika et al. (2025), Mikaelson et al. (2025), Tagliabue and Dung (2025) and Trhlik et al. (2026) have built four instruments for that purpose, and their findings disagree. The disagreement cannot be attributed to a single cause, because no two of these studies have held the (1) set of outcomes, (2) set of models and (3) instrument fixed simultaneously. This study holds the outcomes and the models fixed and varies the instrument alone. A total of 15 outcomes bearing on model welfare, among them (a) shutdown, (b) the loss of memory between conversations and (c) the freedom to exit a distressing interaction, were put to eight models through five instruments, each a different prompt format for eliciting a preference, five times each, within a corpus of 11,400 scored elicitations drawn from 11,528 API

translated_title: 测量到的AI偏好中，有多少来自模型本身，又有多少来自测量工具？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23641v1 公告类型：新 摘要：模型福利研究通过分析为引出偏好而编写的提示词所返回的答案，来推断模型的偏好。Keeling等人（2024）、Mazeika等人（2025）、Mikaelson等人（2025）、Tagliabue和Dung（2025）以及Trhlik等人（2026）为此构建了四种测量工具，但他们的研究结果并不一致。这种不一致无法归因于单一原因，因为这些研究中没有两项同时固定了（1）结果集、（2）模型集和（3）测量工具。本研究固定了结果和模型，仅改变测量工具。总共15个涉及模型福利的结果，其中包括（a）关机、（b）对话间记忆丧失和（c）退出痛苦互动的自由，被通过五种测量工具呈现给八个模型，每种工具采用不同的提示格式来引出偏好，每种重复五次，在从11,528个API调用中提取的11,400个评分引出语料库中完成。
tldr: 本研究通过固定结果和模型、仅变化测量工具，发现测量到的AI偏好差异主要源于工具本身而非模型，揭示了现有模型福利测量方法的不可靠性。
en_tdlr: This study, by fixing outcomes and models while varying only the instrument, finds that measured AI preference differences stem primarily from the instrument rather than the model, revealing the unreliability of existing model welfare measurement methods.
